chapters.title: Two Miraculous Births Foretold
chapters.synopsis: The angel Gabriel promises the aged Zacharias a son named John, then announces to the virgin Mary that she will bear the Son of God. Mary visits Elisabeth, who blesses her, and Mary answers with the Magnificat, magnifying the Lord who exalts the lowly. John the Baptist is born, and his father prophesies that the child will prepare the way of the Lord.

chapters.title: The Babe of Bethlehem
chapters.synopsis: Mary and Joseph travel to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born and laid in a manger, and angels declare good tidings of great joy to shepherds. At the temple, Simeon and Anna recognize the infant as the promised salvation of Israel. Twelve years later the boy Jesus is found in the temple about his Father's business, growing in wisdom and favor.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Wilderness
chapters.synopsis: John the Baptist preaches repentance and baptism along the Jordan, warning that the axe is laid at the root of the trees. He baptizes Jesus, upon whom the Holy Ghost descends as the Father declares him his beloved Son. Luke traces Jesus's lineage back through David and Abraham to Adam.

chapters.title: Tempted, Anointed, and Rejected
chapters.synopsis: After fasting forty days, Jesus repels the devil's temptations with scripture. In the Nazareth synagogue he reads Isaiah's prophecy of the Messiah and declares it fulfilled, but his own townspeople try to cast him off a cliff. He moves to Capernaum, where he teaches with authority, casts out devils, and heals the sick.

chapters.title: Nets Filled and Sinners Called
chapters.synopsis: At Jesus's word Peter lets down his nets and hauls in a miraculous catch, and the fishermen forsake all to follow him. Jesus cleanses a leper and forgives and heals a palsied man lowered through the roof. He calls Levi the publican and teaches that he came to call sinners to repentance.

chapters.title: Apostles Chosen, Beatitudes Spoken
chapters.synopsis: Jesus declares himself Lord of the sabbath and heals a withered hand despite the watching scribes. After a night of prayer he chooses twelve apostles. On a plain he blesses the poor and persecuted, commands love for enemies, and teaches that a true disciple builds on the rock by hearing and doing his sayings.

chapters.title: Faith Great and Love Greater
chapters.synopsis: Jesus marvels at a centurion whose faith exceeds any in Israel and heals his servant from afar, then raises the widow of Nain's son from his bier. He assures John the Baptist's messengers with his miracles and testifies that none born of women is greater than John. In a Pharisee's house a weeping woman anoints his feet, and Jesus teaches that her many sins are forgiven because she loved much.

chapters.title: The Sower, the Storm, the Sleeping Child
chapters.synopsis: Jesus teaches the parable of the sower, explaining how the word of God fares in different hearts. He stills a raging storm on the lake and frees a man possessed by a legion of devils. Returning, he heals a woman who touches his hem in faith and raises the daughter of Jairus from death.

chapters.title: Confession, Transfiguration, and the Cross
chapters.synopsis: Jesus sends the twelve to preach and heal, then feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fishes. Peter confesses him as the Christ of God, and on the mount Jesus is transfigured while Moses and Elias speak with him and the Father's voice owns him. He teaches that whoever would follow him must take up his cross daily, and he sets his face steadfastly toward Jerusalem.

chapters.title: The Good Samaritan
chapters.synopsis: Jesus sends seventy disciples ahead of him two by two, and they return rejoicing that even devils are subject to them. When a lawyer asks who his neighbour is, Jesus answers with the parable of the good Samaritan, who shows mercy where priest and Levite pass by. At Bethany, Martha is cumbered with serving while Mary chooses the good part at Jesus's feet.

chapters.title: Teach Us to Pray
chapters.synopsis: Jesus gives his disciples the Lord's prayer and promises that the Father gives good gifts to those who ask, seek, and knock. Accused of casting out devils by Beelzebub, he answers that a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand. He pronounces woes on Pharisees and lawyers who clean the outside of the cup while neglecting judgment and the love of God.

chapters.title: Treasure in Heaven, Not Barns
chapters.synopsis: Jesus warns against the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and teaches that nothing hidden shall remain unrevealed. He tells of a rich fool whose full barns cannot ransom his soul, then bids his disciples take no thought for their life, for the Father delights to give them the kingdom. He calls all to be watchful servants, ready for their Lord's return.

chapters.title: Except Ye Repent
chapters.synopsis: Jesus teaches that all must repent or perish and tells of a barren fig tree given one more year to bear fruit. He heals a bowed-down woman on the sabbath and likens the kingdom to a mustard seed and leaven. Urging his hearers to strive to enter the strait gate, he laments over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets sent to gather her.

chapters.title: Bidden to the Great Supper
chapters.synopsis: Dining with Pharisees on the sabbath, Jesus heals a man and teaches guests to take the lowest room and hosts to invite the poor. He tells of a great supper whose invited guests all make excuses, so the master fills his house from the highways and hedges. Turning to the multitude, he warns that discipleship demands counting the cost and bearing one's cross.

chapters.title: The Prodigal Son Comes Home
chapters.synopsis: When Pharisees murmur that Jesus receives sinners, he answers with three parables of the lost: the shepherd who leaves ninety and nine for one sheep, the woman who sweeps her house for one coin, and the father who runs to embrace his returning prodigal son. Each ends in joy, for heaven rejoices over one sinner that repenteth. The elder brother's grudging heart is gently answered: it was meet to make merry, for the lost is found.

chapters.title: Mammon and the Beggar Lazarus
chapters.synopsis: Jesus tells of an unjust steward whose shrewdness shames the children of light, teaching that no servant can serve both God and mammon. To the covetous Pharisees he recounts the rich man who ignored the beggar Lazarus at his gate and awoke in torment across a great gulf. Those who hear not Moses and the prophets will not be persuaded though one rose from the dead.

chapters.title: Ten Cleansed, One Grateful
chapters.synopsis: Jesus teaches boundless forgiveness and that faith like a grain of mustard seed can uproot trees. Ten lepers are cleansed on the way to the priests, but only a Samaritan returns to give glory to God. Asked when the kingdom comes, Jesus answers that it is within and warns that his day will overtake the careless as in the days of Noah and Lot.

chapters.title: Prayers, Children, and a Blind Man
chapters.synopsis: Jesus teaches persistence in prayer through the importunate widow and humility through the publican who is justified over the boasting Pharisee. He blesses little children and invites a rich young ruler to sell all and follow him, observing how hard riches make entry into the kingdom. Foretelling his death a third time, he nears Jericho and gives sight to a blind beggar whose faith saves him.

chapters.title: Zacchaeus and the Triumphal Entry
chapters.synopsis: Jesus calls Zacchaeus down from the sycomore tree and declares salvation come to his house, for the Son of man is come to seek and save the lost. He tells the parable of the pounds, requiring servants to improve what their lord entrusts. Riding into Jerusalem amid hosannas, he weeps over the city that knew not its day of visitation and casts the merchants from the temple.

chapters.title: Questions in the Temple
chapters.synopsis: Chief priests demand to know by what authority Jesus acts, and he answers with the parable of the wicked husbandmen who slay the vineyard lord's son. Spies fail to snare him over tribute, for he bids them render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's. He silences the Sadducees on the resurrection, testifying that God is not the God of the dead but of the living.

chapters.title: Signs Before the Son Comes
chapters.synopsis: Jesus declares that a poor widow's two mites outweigh the rich men's gifts. He foretells the destruction of the temple and Jerusalem, the persecution of his disciples, and the signs in sun, moon, and stars that will precede his coming in a cloud with power and great glory. He bids his followers watch and pray, that they may stand before the Son of man.

chapters.title: The Last Supper and Gethsemane
chapters.synopsis: Judas covenants to betray Jesus, who keeps the passover with the twelve and institutes the sacrament of bread and wine in remembrance of his body and blood. In Gethsemane he prays in agony until his sweat falls as great drops of blood, an angel strengthening him. He is betrayed with a kiss, Peter denies him thrice before the cock crows, and the council condemns him for declaring himself the Son of God.

chapters.title: Crucified Between Two Malefactors
chapters.synopsis: Pilate and Herod find no fault in Jesus, yet the multitude demands Barabbas and Jesus is delivered to be crucified. On the cross he pleads forgiveness for his executioners and promises paradise to the penitent thief beside him. Darkness covers the land as he commends his spirit to the Father and dies, and his body is laid in a new sepulchre before the sabbath.

chapters.title: The Road to Emmaus
chapters.synopsis: Women find the tomb empty and angels declare that the Lord is risen. On the road to Emmaus the risen Jesus walks unrecognized with two disciples, expounding all the scriptures concerning himself until their hearts burn and he is known in the breaking of bread. He appears to the gathered disciples, eats before them to prove he has flesh and bones, commissions them as witnesses, and ascends toward heaven in blessing.
